modelSettings.title: Model settings
modelSettings.description: Recommended values are based on this model and system memory. Review them before applying.
modelSettings.estimatedMemoryTooltip: The combined model, KV cache, and runtime buffer calculated from downloaded metadata and the current context setting. Actual usage may vary by runtime and system state.
modelSettings.automaticSetupGgufTooltip:
Vyact automatic runtime settings (GGUF)
GPU offload: Automatic
Memory fitting: Automatic
Concurrent generation: 1
Flash Attention: Automatic
Prompt cache: Enabled
RoPE, mmap, KV GPU offload: llama.cpp defaults
modelSettings.automaticSetupMlxTooltip:
Vyact automatic runtime settings (MLX)
Metal execution: Managed by the MLX runtime
Prompt cache (APC): Enabled
Batch, threads, and memory management: MLX defaults
modelSettings.contextTooltip: The maximum amount of conversation and document text the model can consider at once. Larger values use more memory. Keep the recommended value unless long inputs are being cut off.
modelSettings.maxOutputTooltip: The maximum length of one response. Increasing it allows longer answers but takes more time and leaves less room for the conversation context.
modelSettings.historyTokenBudgetTooltip: The maximum amount of earlier conversation this model can receive with each request. This value is a ceiling; the actual amount may be smaller depending on the model's context size and the space used by the system prompt, current question, attached documents, and reserved output. Increase it when the model forgets older messages; reduce it to leave more room for the current input.
modelSettings.temperatureTooltip: Controls randomness. Lower values are more consistent and factual; higher values are more varied and creative. 0.2 is a safe general-purpose value.
modelSettings.topKTooltip: Limits each next-token choice to the K most likely candidates. Leave it at the model default unless you understand sampling controls.
modelSettings.topPTooltip: Chooses from the smallest group of likely tokens whose combined probability reaches this value. Leave it at the model default for normal use.
modelSettings.gpuManualSplitOffHelp: Off · Recommended. llama.cpp automatically fits the model to available GPU memory for the more stable setup.
modelSettings.gpuManualSplitOnHelp: On · Uses the values below as a fixed split ratio. Automatic memory fitting is limited and an unsuitable split may fail to load.
modelSettings.gpuManualSplitTooltip: OFF leaves tensor allocation to llama.cpp --fit and is the safer default. ON sends a manual --tensor-split percentage for each GPU; the total must be 100%.
modelSettings.gpuAllocationHelp: Estimated from each compatible GPU's VRAM ratio. Adjust only when balancing multiple GPUs.
modelSettings.gpuAllocationTooltip: Each value is a llama.cpp tensor split percentage with up to two decimal places, and the total must be 100%. It is not a hard VRAM usage limit.
modelSettings.gpuSplitInvalid: Set the GPU split percentages to a total of 100%.
modelSettings.gpuSplitCapacityWarning: At this ratio, GPU {{index}} may receive about {{required}}, exceeding its {{capacity}} VRAM. Actual llama.cpp allocation may differ, but the model may fail to load. Use the recommended ratio or turn off manual splitting.
modelSettings.mtpAccelerationHelp: Speeds up generation with the model's MTP predictor. Turn it off to use KV cache quantization.
modelSettings.omlxMtpAccelerationHelp: Uses the installed compatible external MTP draft through oMLX. Memory Cache remains enabled.
modelSettings.dflash2AccelerationHelp: DFlash2 is detected and enabled automatically for this model.
modelSettings.dflash2AccelerationTooltip: Runs a compatible DFlash2 draft through llama.cpp or oMLX. Only one speculative acceleration path is enabled at a time.
modelSettings.mtpAccelerationTooltip: MTP lets a compatible model predict several tokens ahead and can improve generation speed. It uses an additional predictor and cannot be combined with KV cache quantization in Vyact.
modelSettings.omlxMtpAccelerationTooltip: External MTP is used without SpecPrefill or native MTP. Only a compatible installed draft is selected.
modelSettings.cacheQuantizationHelp: Reduces cache memory use for larger contexts.
modelSettings.cacheQuantizationMtpHelp: Turn off MTP acceleration to enable KV cache quantization.
modelSettings.accelerationConflict: MTP acceleration and KV cache quantization cannot be enabled together.

mtpFailures.load_failed: MTP could not be loaded in this environment, so the model is running without it.
mtpFailures.out_of_memory: MTP could not be loaded because there was not enough memory, so the model is running without it.

modelSettings.performanceModeHelp: Adjusts llama.cpp batching for speed or lower memory use.
modelSettings.performanceModeTooltip: Auto uses Vyact's balanced defaults. Memory saving reduces temporary processing memory. Maximum performance uses larger batches and may require more memory.
modelSettings.cpuThreadsHelp: Limits llama.cpp CPU usage. Leave empty for automatic selection.
modelSettings.cpuThreadsTooltip: Sets how many CPU threads llama.cpp may use. A lower value reduces CPU load and heat but may slow generation. Leave empty unless you need to limit resource use.
modelSettings.kvCachePrecisionHelp: Q8 preserves more precision; Q4 uses less memory.
modelSettings.kvCachePrecisionTooltip: The KV cache stores the model's working memory for the current context. Q8 saves memory with a small quality tradeoff; Q4 saves more memory but can affect quality more. It cannot be used with MTP.
modelSettings.seedHelp: Leave empty for random. To reproduce results, enter any integer from 0 to 2,147,483,647 (for example, 42).
modelSettings.seedTooltip: A seed is the starting number for response randomness; the number itself does not improve performance or quality. You can use any integer from 0 to 2,147,483,647. Using the same seed makes results easier to reproduce when the input and all other settings are identical. Leave it empty to use a random seed for each request.

modelBenchmark.title: Performance test
modelBenchmark.restore_failed: Restore failed. Select your model again.
modelBenchmark.save_failed: Measurement completed, but saving failed. Retry saving the result.
modelBenchmark.requestFailed: Request failed. Retry after other work finishes. A running test will reappear when reconnected.
modelBenchmark.case_failed: This configuration could not be measured.
modelBenchmark.settings_changed: Excluded: runtime changed the requested settings.
modelBenchmark.selected: Selected test settings filled in. Review the highlighted changes, then press Apply.
modelBenchmark.description: Compare performance mode, KV precision and supported MTP at the current context. Model reloads can take time.
modelBenchmark.fixed: CPU threads, GPU split, context and sampling stay fixed. Uses synthetic text; answer quality is not evaluated.
modelBenchmark.restoreNotice: Chat and setting changes pause during testing. Stopping ends the request and restores the original model.
modelBenchmark.comparisonNotice: Prefill and generation rates use engine-reported measurements. Unavailable metrics are shown as unavailable. Retest after changing the environment or settings.
modelBenchmark.mlxPrefill: This MLX engine does not report a separate prefill duration. It is unavailable, rather than substituted with first-token time.
modelBenchmark.remaining: About {{minutes}} min of measurements left · excludes reloads and additional checks
modelBenchmark.scoreNotice: Each selected combination runs short input, long input and follow-up once. Comparison uses first-token time and generation rate and applies only to these test conditions.
modelBenchmark.stale: Environment or fixed settings differ from this run. Retest under current conditions.
modelBenchmark.replaceWarning: Starting a new test deletes previous results for this model. Finished measurements are saved immediately and retained if stopped.
modelBenchmark.comparisonFields: Compared settings: {{fields}}. Other settings stay fixed; model reloading may take time.
modelBenchmark.currentOnly: Only one configuration is available, so this measures its performance.
modelBenchmark.dflashNotice: DFlash2 is applied automatically to compatible models and stays enabled during testing. On/off comparison is not performed.
